summary.plain: KATRIN's most precise measurement yet shows that neutrinos weigh no more than 0.45 electron-volts — nearly twice as tight a bound as its previous result, still finding no sign of an actual mass.
summary.technical: Based on the first five KATRIN neutrino-mass measurement campaigns (259 measurement days, 36 million electrons near the tritium beta-decay endpoint), the best-fit mν² = -0.14(+0.13/-0.15) eV² yields an upper limit mν < 0.45 eV at 90% CL, improving KATRIN's previous bound by a factor of almost two.

title: Direct neutrino-mass measurement based on 259 days of KATRIN data
why_it_matters: This is the tightest model-independent, laboratory (non-cosmological) upper limit yet placed on the absolute mass of the neutrino, using only kinematics of a well-understood nuclear decay.
